events.title: Optometrist Q&A Session
events.description:
👀 Hey Pre-Optometry Club! We are so excited to announce our next event! We will be hosting an Optometrist Q&A session with our guest speaker, Dr. Jason Chau! 

Join us on Monday, November 23rd at 7:00 PM in STC 0020 for an opportunity to learn more about the field of optometry, hear about Dr. Chau’s journey from optometry school to clinical practice, and gain insight into what it’s like to own and operate an optometry clinic!

Grab your friends, get your questions ready, and come join us for an evening of great conversations, food, and refreshments!

🔗Sign up using the link in our bio :)

Get to know our speaker:

Dr. Jason Chau is an optometrist and Clinic Director at Innovation Eye Clinic, a modern optometry practice located in downtown Kitchener, Ontario. He earned his Doctor of Optometry (OD) degree from the University of Waterloo and has a special interest in dry eye therapy, myopia management, and orthokeratology (Ortho-K). After graduating, Dr. Chau gained experience in ocular research at the Centre for Ocular Research & Education (CORE). In 2023, he opened Innovation Eye Clinic with the goal of providing personalized, patient-centred eye care through advanced diagnostic technology and evidence-based treatments. Dr. Chau is passionate about patient education and combining innovative approaches to eye care with meaningful patient relationships.

We can’t wait to see you there! 💙👁️

Nance Lab Tour – Mon, Nov 23 at Benson Hall (time TBD). Explore how the team combines neuroscience, nanotechnology, data science, and imaging to develop treatments for neurological disorders, with a focus on brain health in newborns and children.

WHOOOO is ready for the Association for Computing Education (ACE) monthly book club, README.ace: December Selection! 🦉 📖

At each meeting, we will facilitate deep discussion on a new computing education paper/media. The environment will be calming and welcoming, with comforting drinks, such as hot tea and hot cocoa, alongside embrace from our owl plushies. And excitingly, every book club attended will earn an entry into our exclusive end-of-year book club raffle! 

For this meeting, we will be exploring the paper “Deconstructing Conceptions of Rigor in Computer Science Education” (Everson et al.), to explore how students and instructors perceive “rigor” differently, and its subsequent effect in the classroom.

This event is open to everyone; the ACE team welcomes you!

📅 Date: Wednesday, December 2nd
🕔 Time: 5:00 PM - 6:00 PM
📍 Location: CSE1 403 (Allen)
*Please remember to RSVP at the link in our bio!*

- ACE Officers

If you have any questions or concerns, please don’t hesitate to contact us at ace-officers@cs.washington.edu. ACE is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation for our events, programs, activities, and education for individuals with disabilities (with advance notice). Please reach out to Linda Taing, Senior Student Leadership Development Specialist, directly at lindavt@cs.washington.edu if you have any questions or requests.

events.title: Accessibility Audit - Wallingford
events.description:
UAG welcomes any and all interested students to join us for our Accessibility (Walk) Audit of the Wallingford neighborhood of Seattle. We will be convening in the parking lot of the Burke museum at the start time, then we will travel as a group to the start location.
We will be using an app to record the infrastructure accessibility of a section of the neighborhood. This data can then be used for awareness and advocacy purposes, as well as being integrated into a tool that allows people with mobility impairments plan urban routes that accommodate their specific accessibility needs.
Mostly, these audits are about raising awareness about urban accessibility and enjoying a walk with other great people. Volunteer hours are provided to all participants.

events.title: Yoga Teacher Training
events.description:
Ready to take your yoga practice to the next level? 🧘‍♀️ UW Recreation is offering our 200-hour Yoga Teacher Training this winter! The program is a great opportunity to deepen your practice, develop your teaching skills, and earn a Yoga Alliance RYS 200 certification.

📅 January 9 - March 14, 2027
📍 Studio 316, IMA 
* More information regarding dates and times is in the  link provided 

Hear from one of our instructors who recently completed the YTT program! 🌟

“Hi, my name is Carmela and I am a yoga instructor at the IMA. I graduated a few months ago from the University of Washington’s Yoga Teacher Training program. As a student and a long time practitioner of yoga, I needed a training that would fit into my schedule while still showing me the depth inherent to yoga. The UW program felt tailored to students and I was able to attend the weekly classes all quarter, forming connections with other students, while keeping up with classes and work expectations. I enjoyed the program’s emphasis on the historical roots of asana and spiritual practices as well as the posture workshops where we dove into the minutia of primary poses. If you are a UW student looking to deepen your practice without sacrificing other areas of your life, the IMA YTT may be for you!” - Carmela Leache

Registration is open! Follow link below to sign up today.

https://www.washington.edu/ima/yoga-teacher-training/

#YTT #yoga #uw #ima #2027goals
